segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Hi Thomas, how are you enjoying the course so far?

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Yeah, I think it’s good.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Remind me - why did you decide to study sports science? Didn't you want to be a professional athlete when you were at school?

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Yeah - that was my goal, and all my classmates assumed I would achieve it; they /22 thought I was brilliant.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: That must have been a nice feeling.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Mm, I thought I could win anything. There was no one who could run faster than me.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Exactly - so what happened? Did your mum and dad want you to be more ‘academic’?

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Not at all. Perhaps they should have pushed me harder, though. /22

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: What do you mean?

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: I think I should have practised more.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: What makes you say that?

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Well, I went out to Kenya for a couple of weeks to train ...

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Really! I didn’t know that.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: I was chosen to go there out of loads of kids and run with some of the top teenage athletes in the world. And ... I was so calm about it. I just kept thinking /24 how fortunate I was. What a great chance this was! Everyone back home was so proud of me. But once we started competing, I very quickly realised I wasn’t good enough.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: That must have been a huge shock.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: I thought ‘this can’t be happening’! I was used to winning. /24

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: I'm sorry to hear that.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: It’s OK. I'm over it now and I think it's much better to do a university course and this one has such a variety of sports-related areas. It’s going to be good.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Oh, I agree - I chose it because of that.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: So Jeanne - have you thought of any ideas for the discussion session next week on technology and sport?

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: We have to cover more than one sport, don't we?

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Yeah.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: You know - we always think technology is about the future, but we could gather some ideas about past developments in sport.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Look at early types of equipment perhaps? Uh, I remember reading something about table tennis bats once - how they ended up being covered with pimpled rubber.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Cos they were just wooden at first, I’d imagine.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Yeah. In about the 1920s, a factory was making rolls of the rubber in bulk for something like horse harnesses.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Really!

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Yeah - and someone realised that it’d make a perfect covering for the wooden bats.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: So what about cricket - that’s had a few innovative changes. Maybe the pads they wear on their legs? thomas: I don't think they've changed much but, I’m just looking on the internet ... and it says that when the first cricket helmet came in, in 1978. the Australian batsman who first wore it was booed and jeered by people watching because it was so ugly!

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Wow, players have to protect themselves from getting hurt! I mean everyone wears one now.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Mm, unlike the cycle helmet.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Well, unless you're a professional, but you’re right, many ordinary bikers don't wear a helmet.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Hey, look at these pictures of original helmet designs. This one looks like an upside-down bowl!

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Yet, the woman’s laughing - she’s so proud to be wearing it!

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: It says serious cyclists ended up with wet hair from all the hard exercise.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: I guess that's why they have large air vents in them now so that the skin can breathe more easily.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: OK, so we’ve done helmets. What about golf balls or better still golf clubs - they’ve changed a lot.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Yeah - I remember my great grandfather telling me that because a club was made entirely of wood, it would easily break and players had to get another.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: There's no wood at all in them now, is there?

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: No - they’re much more powerful.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: The same must be true of hockey sticks.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: I don’t think so because players still use wooden sticks today. What it does say here, though, is that when the game started you had to produce a stick yourself. 029 thomas: I guess they just weren’t being manufactured. So, one more perhaps. What about football?

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Well, I know the first balls were made of animal skin.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Yeah, they covered them with pieces of leather that were stitched together, but... the balls let in water when it rained.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: Oh, that would have made them much heavier.

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: That’s right. You can imagine the damage to players’ necks when the ball was headed.

segments.speaker: JEANNE
segments.en: How painful that must have been!

segments.speaker: THOMAS
segments.en: Yeah, well, I think we can put together some useful ideas ...
